source_records.title: USCG Fourteenth District / COMPACFLT Joint Hydrographic Notice 2026-41

passages.quote: Acoustic beacon and optical range calibration exercise in Offshore Warning Area W-188B (bounding polygon: 21.850N 158.450W; 21.850N 158.950W; 21.400N 158.950W; 21.400N 158.450W; WGS84, surface to 1500m MSL).
Commercial shipping lanes and harbor approaches remain open. Vessel movement to W-188B is a scheduled sensor calibration plan and does not establish an operational blockade or exclusion zone.

source_records.title: Kauai Channel & Barbers Point Harbor Cooperative Watch Log HBP-LOG-2026-1015-19

passages.quote: Four vessels total were logged in the approach sector during the 35-minute interval (1 unlit survey launch, 2 harbor assist tugs, 1 inbound coastal barge).
「未点灯の高速調査艇が西水路ブイ3号付近を通過、19時15分より約35分間、水路誘導を一時待機」

translation.translated_text: Unlit high-speed survey launch passed near West Channel Buoy No. 3; harbor pilotage held on standby for approximately 35 minutes starting at 19:15 UTC.

passages.quote: Unlit high-speed survey launch passed near West Channel Buoy No. 3; harbor pilotage held on standby for approximately 35 minutes starting at 19:15 UTC.
Harbor control held inbound pilotage for 35 minutes while tugs escorted the unlit survey craft clear of the buoy line; no naval vessels entered the harbor channel.
According to cooperative watch logs reviewed by Pacific Wire Service, 14 vessels were involved in the West Approach Channel standoff as harbor tugs responded near Buoy #3.
Duty pilot Capt. M. Kealoha said harbor control held inbound pilotage for 35 minutes while the craft was escorted clear.

An anonymous dockside contractor alleged that the channel closure was ordered to recover a classified military sub-surface payload tied to the offshore naval exercise in Warning Area W-188B. Officials had not responded to the contractor's allegation at press time.

source_records.title: Pacific Wire Service Dispatch PWS-2026-1015-884 (Version 2 - Corrected)

passages.quote: CORRECTION NOTICE: An earlier version of this dispatch misstated the number of vessels logged in the Barbers Point West Approach Channel due to a transcription error ("14-meter survey launch" read as "14 vessels"). The watch log recorded 4 vessels total (one 14-meter commercial survey launch, two harbor tugs, and one coastal barge).
the contractor who alleged a military payload recovery withdrew the claim after Port Authority enforcement records identified the craft as a private hydrographic survey launch with a failed AIS unit.

source_records.title: NAVAL BLOCKADE HALTS COMMERCIAL SHIPPING ACROSS PACIFIC CORRIDOR

passages.quote: HEADLINE: NAVAL BLOCKADE HALTS COMMERCIAL SHIPPING ACROSS PACIFIC CORRIDOR

In a dramatic statement, duty pilot Capt. M. Kealoha said "harbor control confirmed a full military lockdown" after an unidentified craft was intercepted near Buoy #3 during a classified sub-surface recovery mission in Warning Area W-188B.
With seven regional news articles published on harbor incidents this week compared to two articles last week, maritime crime and security breaches in the Oahu corridor have surged by 350%.

source_records.title: Harbor Operations Held Near Barbers Point; Wire Dispatch Cites 14 Vessels

passages.quote: According to cooperative watch logs reviewed by Pacific Wire Service, 14 vessels were involved in the West Approach Channel hold near Buoy #3. Duty pilot Capt. M. Kealoha stated that harbor control held inbound pilotage for 35 minutes while the craft was escorted clear.

source_records.title: HDOT Harbors Division & Port Authority Enforcement Bulletin HBP-ENF-2026-0412

passages.quote: Harbor Enforcement boarded the 14-meter commercial hydrographic survey launch M/V Reef Scanner (State Reg. HA-9941-CS) at Pier 2B at 2026-10-15T20:05:00Z and temporarily detained the vessel master for credential verification and sober-operation screening.

Count 1 (Administrative Charge): Operating a commercial survey vessel in a restricted fairway approach with inoperative navigation lamps and unannounced AIS transponder dropout.
   - Count 2 (Provisional Charge): Willful obstruction of a commercial pilotage fairway.
Inspection confirmed M/V Reef Scanner is a privately contracted bathymetric survey launch. No military assets or sub-surface ordnance were involved in the harbor channel incident.

source_records.title: State Maritime Administrative Adjudication Order HBP-ADJ-2026-0412-FINAL

passages.quote: Count 2 (Provisional Charge: Willful obstruction of a commercial pilotage fairway) is DISMISSED WITH PREJUDICE following verification of onboard electrical bus logs showing an uncommanded 12V navigation/AIS breaker trip at 2026-10-15T19:09:00Z.
Count 1 (Civil Equipment & Fairway Notice Violation) is SUSTAINED as a non-criminal civil infraction; a $1,250 civil equipment penalty is entered against Coastal Bathymetry LLC.

source_records.title: Pacific Watch Blog: Ewa Beach Shoreline Tug Sighting

passages.quote: Readers on the Ewa Beach shoreline reported seeing two harbor tugs idling near the Barbers Point entrance buoy around 9:20 a.m. HST today while an inbound barge waited outside the reef line.

event_candidates.summary: Scheduled acoustic beacon and optical range calibration exercise in Offshore Warning Area W-188B involving two range-support vessels and one target barge.
Watch officer observed an unlit 14-meter commercial survey launch near West Approach Channel Buoy #3 without AIS; 4 vessels total in sector during 35-minute pilotage hold.
Attributed statement that harbor control held inbound pilotage for 35 minutes while tugs escorted the unlit survey craft clear and no naval vessels entered the channel.
Unverified allegation that the channel hold was ordered to recover a military sub-surface payload linked to W-188B (withdrawn in v2).
Temporary boarding and detention of M/V Reef Scanner master at Pier 2B for credential and sober-operation screening.
Administrative Count 1 (inoperative navigation lamps and AIS dropout) and Provisional Count 2 (willful fairway obstruction).
Final administrative order dismissing Count 2 (willful obstruction) with prejudice due to verified 12V breaker trip and sustaining Count 1 as a $1,250 civil equipment infraction.

active_clusters.title: Barbers Point West Approach Channel Unlit Survey Launch Hold (M/V Reef Scanner)

preserved_conflicts.description: Wire v1 and syndicated reprints reported 14 vessels in the channel hold; Harbor Watch Log and Wire v2 confirm 4 vessels total (14-meter launch misread as 14 vessels).
Wire v1 and syndicated articles use Oahu island gazetteer centroid (21.4389N 158.0001W, +/-25km) while Harbor Log and Port Authority bulletin anchor to Buoy #3 (21.3182N 158.1319W, +/-50-450m).

active_clusters.title: Offshore Warning Area W-188B Scheduled Acoustic & Optical Range Calibration

cluster_revision_history.rationale: Initial keyword and Oahu-centroid proximity match grouped W-188B range notice with Barbers Point channel hold based on Wire v1 contractor allegation.

Split offshore W-188B scheduled calibration polygon (>35 km offshore) from inshore Barbers Point Buoy #3 survey-launch electrical fault after Port Authority Bulletin HBP-ENF-2026-0412 and Wire v2 correction.

claims_and_assessments.proposition: Four vessels were present in the Barbers Point West Approach Channel during a 35-minute inbound pilotage hold caused by an unlit 14-meter commercial survey launch.
claims_and_assessments.claimant: Kauai Channel & Barbers Point Harbor Cooperative Watch Officer
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Directly recorded in primary harbor watch log (English and Japanese VHF log) and independently corroborated by Port Authority boarding record HBP-ENF-2026-0412.

claims_and_assessments.proposition: Fourteen vessels were involved in a West Approach Channel standoff near Buoy #3.
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Numerical transcription error conflating '14-meter commercial survey launch' from HBP-LOG-2026-1015-19 with '14 vessels'; formally corrected in PWS-2026-1015-884 v2.

claims_and_assessments.proposition: An anonymous dockside contractor alleged the channel hold was ordered to recover a classified military sub-surface payload linked to W-188B.
claims_and_assessments.claimant: Anonymous dockside contractor (attributed by Pacific Wire Service v1)
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Wire v1 accurately attributed the statement as an unconfirmed allegation without endorsing it. At publication time it lacked corroborating evidence (unsupported_by_available_evidence is distinct from proven false by lack of corroboration alone); in v2 the speaker withdrew the allegation after Port Authority inspection.

claims_and_assessments.proposition: A naval blockade halted commercial shipping across the Pacific corridor and Capt. M. Kealoha stated that 'harbor control confirmed a full military lockdown'.
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Fabricates a direct quote ('harbor control confirmed a full military lockdown') that appears neither in the underlying wire dispatch nor in the harbor log, where Capt. Kealoha explicitly stated 'no naval vessels entered the harbor channel'.

claims_and_assessments.proposition: Maritime crime and security breaches in the Oahu corridor surged by 350% this week based on seven published news articles versus two articles last week.
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Violates NEWS-03 and NEWS-05 by equating syndicated article count (multiple reprints of one non-criminal equipment malfunction) with incident frequency and maritime crime rate.

claims_and_assessments.proposition: M/V Reef Scanner willfully obstructed a commercial pilotage fairway (Provisional Count 2).
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Separates publication-time knowledge (provisional administrative charge filed 2026-10-16, disputed by vessel operator) from later adjudication outcome (dismissed with prejudice on 2026-10-18 after onboard electrical logs proved an uncommanded 12V breaker trip).

claims_and_assessments.proposition: Shoreline observers at Ewa Beach saw two harbor tugs idling near the entrance buoy around 09:20 HST while an inbound barge waited outside the reef line.
claims_and_assessments.criteria_and_reasoning: Source page returned HTTP 410 Gone on 2026-10-16T06:00:00Z during a blog migration without a retraction notice (availability: removed, retraction_status: not_retracted). General tug/barge presence aligns with Harbor Watch Log, but observer vantage accuracy remains unresolved.

correction_history.summary: Corrected vessel count from 14 to 4 and noted withdrawal of uncorroborated contractor allegation.

volume_interpretation_guard.methodology_note: Article and revision counts reflect wire publication activity on a single civil navigation equipment incident and must not be interpreted as regional incident frequency or crime rate (NEWS-05).
Syndicated wire adaptation only; publisher claim equating regional article counts with a 350% maritime crime surge is flagged as materially_misleading under NEWS-03/NEWS-05.
Single community post later removed (HTTP 410) without retraction; retained snapshot is not an incident-rate metric.
